name: Jellyfin Federation
description: Aggregate content from multiple Jellyfin servers into unified virtual libraries
overview: The Jellyfin Federation Plugin allows you to create a unified media library by aggregating content from multiple remote Jellyfin servers. Stream content from any server without file synchronization.
changelog: Wider bug/QoL sweep of the rest of the codebase (found via a dedicated review pass, each verified before fixing - not a guess-and-patch list): (1) PluginConfiguration.GloballyExcludedItemIds (the 'stop sharing this item with everyone' list) was missing from the config-save preservation block - saving any unrelated setting silently un-excluded every item an admin had explicitly stopped sharing. Same bug class as 0.0.104's AllowedExternalLibraryIds gap. (2) 'Download to server' deleted the local virtual item but never told the sync engine to stop re-fetching it, so the very next scheduled refresh recreated the same item as a duplicate alongside the real downloaded file - now suppressed via the existing per-item hide list. (3) A per-remote-user rating ceiling (MaxAllowedRating on a friend's AllLibraries/CertainItems/CertainLibraries access rule) was a silent permanent no-op - the rating lookup was a stub that always returned null. Now actually resolves the item's real rating from the federation cache. (4) Changing 'Refresh interval' in this plugin's own settings had no live effect - Jellyfin only reads a scheduled task's trigger from GetDefaultTriggers() once, at first registration, not on every config save. Now pushes the new interval into Jellyfin's live task scheduler on every save. (5) A blocking .GetAwaiter().GetResult() call in the download path is now properly async. Also, stress-testing turned up and fixed a real intermittent bug from 0.0.108's own handle-leak fix: disposing the Tailscale login process from its Exited event could race ahead of the last buffered output line under load (a documented .NET gotcha), occasionally dropping the very login-URL line the feature depends on - disposal now waits for the redirected output streams to actually finish first. 301 tests, all green (2 new this pass, covering the rating-ceiling fix).
